evidence.quote: A mixed sumset problem. (Contributed by I. Laba) Given an integer n 1, how small can jA + Aj be for an n-element set A R and transcendental ? Konyagin and Laba showed in [59] that jA + Aj cn log n=(log log n) with an absolute constant c > 0. On the other hand, an example due to Green (also presented in [59]) shows that jA + Aj necplog n is possible.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $n \geq 1$ be an integer and let $\alpha \in \mathbb{R}$ be a transcendental number. For a finite set $A \subset \mathbb{R}$ with $|A| = n$, define the mixed sumset
$$A + \alpha A = \{a + \alpha a' : a, a' \in A\}.$$
Determine the correct order of magnitude, as $n \to \infty$, of the quantity
$$f(n) = \min_{\substack{A \subset \mathbb{R},\ |A| = n \\ \alpha \in \mathbb{R}\ \text{transcendental}}} |A + \alpha A|.$$
It is known that there exist absolute constants $c_1, c_2 > 0$ such that
$$c_1 \cdot \frac{n \log n}{\log \log n} \;\leq\; f(n) \;\leq\; n \cdot e^{c_2 \sqrt{\log n}}.$$
Close the gap between these bounds, i.e., determine $f(n)$ up to constants in the exponent.
artifact.status_search_result: Conlon and Lim (arXiv:2212.10128, "Sums of transcendental dilates") proved that there is an absolute constant $c > 0$ such that $|A + \lambda A| \geq e^{c\sqrt{\log |A|}}|A|$ for every finite $A \subset \mathbb{R}$ and every transcendental $\lambda$. Combined with the matching upper-bound construction of Konyagin and Łaba (also attributed to Green), this determines $f(n) = n \cdot e^{\Theta(\sqrt{\log n})}$, resolving the problem up to the constant in the exponent.

status_evidence.title: Sums of transcendental dilates
status_evidence.snippet: There is an absolute constant c>0 such that |A+λ·A| ≥ e^{c√log|A|}|A| for any finite subset A of ℝ and any transcendental λ. By a construction of Konyagin and Łaba, this is best possible up to the constant c.
status_evidence.claim: Conlon and Lim establish the matching lower bound, resolving the problem up to the constant in the exponent.

status_evidence.title: Sums of transcendental dilates (Conlon-Lim)
status_evidence.snippet: The problem of giving a lower bound on a sum of the form A + λ·A first occurred in the work of Łaba and Konyagin... we resolve this problem.
status_evidence.claim: The paper explicitly resolves the Konyagin–Łaba problem for transcendental dilates.
